title: West Indies penalised for slow over-rate in second test against Sri Lanka
byline: The West Indies have been fined 10 per cent of their match fee and penalised two ICC World Test Championship points for maintaining a slow over-rate against Sri Lanka in the second Test played in North Sound, Saint George, Antigua and Barbuda.

title: West Indies eye new era after historic Sri Lanka series win
byline: West Indies ended a wait of more than two decades for a Test series victory over Sri Lanka, sealing a memorable 1-0 triumph and raising hopes of a new era under captain Roston Chase.

title: US launches more strikes on Iran with blasts reported in south of country
byline: The US has launched a new round of strikes on Iran after President Donald Trump signalled he’d ’’hit them hard again tonight’’ following an overnight exchange of attacks on Tuesday.

title: Paralympic great Storey retires from GB competition
byline: Dame Sarah Storey, Great Britain’s most-decorated Paralympian, has retired from international competition with immediate effect. The 48-year-old cyclist has opted not to compete at Los Angeles 2028 to focus on helping improve Para-sport.

title: World Cup Quarter-finals Set! Eight Teams, Four Blockbuster Battles
byline: Eight teams remain. Four matches await. Only four will reach the FIFA World Cup 2026 semi-finals.

title: Castle road rail level crossing closed this weekend, Kelani Valley trains restricted
byline: The Castle Road railway level crossing between Baseline and Narahenpita railway stations will be closed to vehicular traffic for 22 hours this weekend due to essential renovation work, the Railways Department said.

title: Sri Lanka, Kazakhstan discuss expanding defence and security ties
byline: The Resident Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of the Republic of Kazakhstan to Sri Lanka Sergey Viktorov, paid a courtesy call on Deputy Minister of Defence Major General Aruna Jayasekara (Retd) and Defence Secretary Air Vice Marshal Sampath Thuyacontha (Retd) at the Ministry of Defence.

title: Old Bogambara prison officially re-designated as prison by gazette
byline: The government has officially re-designated the Old Bogambara prison premises as a prison under the Prisons Ordinance through a Gazette notification issued by Justice and National Integration Minister Harshana Nanayakkara.

title: Indian national among inmates killed in Sri Lanka’s prison riots
byline: An Indian national was among the inmates killed in Sri Lanka’s prison riots on Monday (July 6, 2026), Colombo-based official sources told The Hindu, identifying the victim as Unnikrishnan S., aged 73 years.

title: Colombo university shifts lectures online over dengue
byline: The Colombo University has decided to conduct all lectures online from tomorrow (10) until July 15 due to the ongoing spread of dengue.

title: Jaffna airport control tower upgraded with air situation display system
byline: The Electronics & Air Navigation Engineering (E&ANE) Division of Airport & Aviation Services (Sri Lanka) (Private) Limited (AASL) has successfully implemented an Air Situation Display System at the Jaffna International Airport Control Tower, enhancing air traffic management capabilities.

title: Dengue death toll rises to 45; daily case count tops 1,200
byline: Sri Lanka’s dengue death toll has increased to 45 this year, while the total number of reported cases has climbed to 65,034, the National Dengue Control Unit (NDCU) said.

title: Western Europe records its hottest June as heatwaves surge
byline: Western Europe this year experienced its hottest June on record as a searing heatwave swept across a continent facing increasingly frequent and intense heat extremes, the EU’s climate monitor said on Thursday (July 9, 2026).

title: Sri Lankan Rupee hits Rs. 340 against USD
byline: The Sri Lankan rupee weakened further against the US dollar today, with the dollar’s selling rate crossing the Rs. 340 mark, according to the latest daily exchange rates released by the Central Bank.

title: House of underworld figure ’Thembili Lahiru’ set ablaze in Middeniya
byline: The house of alleged underworld figure known as ’’Thembili Lahiru’’ was set on fire by an unidentified group in the Kudagalara area of Middeniya on Tuesday night (July 8), police said.

title: Couple transforms AC train coach into ‘honeymoon coupe’, Indian Railways takes action
byline: A viral video showing a train’s First AC cabin decorated like a lavish ‘honeymoon suite’ has prompted the Indian Railways to suspend a ticket checker and order an inquiry.

title: Archchuna threatens to remove clothes after Govt MP questions his attire
byline: Independent MP Ramanathan Archchuna in Parliament today threatened to remove his clothes after ruling party MP M. Jeganeeswaran  questioned his attire.

title: LRT project will not be implemented?
byline: The Light Rail Transit (LRT) project is not likely to see the light of the day, Minister of Transport Bimal Ratnayake hinted in Parliament today.

title: Iran launches retaliatory strikes on Gulf states as Trump warns US bombing could get ’much worse’
byline: Air raid sirens sounded in Bahrain and Kuwait overnight after Iran vowed to respond to renewed US strikes on the country.

title: New vehicle registrations to get priority in number plate printing
byline: Priority will be given to vehicles with new registrations when printing and issuing vehicle number plates, Department of Motor Traffic (DMT) Commissioner General Kamal Amarasinghe said.

title: CID probe underway as Excise security stickers found on counterfeit liquor bottles
byline: A Criminal Investigation Department probe is currently underway over a large seizure of counterfeit liquor bottles recently from Malambe had the Excise Department approved security sticker pasted on the bottle necks, thus giving the impression whether the perpetrators have forged the sticker too.

title: No point in associating MR with underworld figures now: MP
byline: In what seemed humorous but a fact at the same time, Opposition MP Chamara Sampath Dassanayake yesterday highlighted that there is no point in associating former President Mahinda Rajapaksa with underworld figures and criticising him as he is no longer engaged in active politics.

title: Sri Lanka to make fresh U.S. engagement to ensure child labour-free export supply chains
byline: Sri Lanka is planning fresh engagements with the United States (U.S.) in a bid to avert new tariffs linked to child or forced labour, with the country’s export authorities seeking to demonstrate that it deals with the possible import of raw materials or intermediary goods tainted with such concerns for export industries, an official said.

title: 1993 murder case finally sees justice
byline: Eight men convicted of murdering a woman by assaulting her with sharp weapons and clubs and causing grievous injuries to two others were today sentenced to death by Colombo High Court Judge Buddhika Sri Ragala.

title: It could have been nipped in the bud. Only if we had been given orders – Prison officer to Minister
byline: A prison officer told Justice Minister Harshana Nanayakkara yesterday that the Negombo prison unrest which claimed the lives of several prison officers and inmates could have been prevented had timely orders been issued to contain the situation.

title: Mulgampola railway crossing to close for repairs from July 10 to 13
byline: The Mulgampola (Randon Hills) railway crossing between Kandy and Peradeniya railway stations will be temporarily closed to vehicular traffic from Friday evening to Monday morning to facilitate essential repair work, the Railways Department said.

title: Tilvin wins copyright case against Wimal
byline: The Supreme Court dismissed an appeal filed by former Parliamentarian Wimal Weerawansa, affirming that he infringed the copyright of Janatha Vimukthi Peramuna (JVP) General Secretary Tilvin Silva by reproducing the book titled ’Neththa Venuwata Aththa’.

title: Refereeing chief denies bias claims in Argentina-Egypt game
byline: FIFA refereeing chief ‌Pierluigi Collina has defended the officiating in Argentina’s dramatic 3-2 victory over Egypt in the World ⁠Cup round of ⁠16, dismissing allegations of bias and saying match officials operated with complete independence.

title: Eight Colombo PHIs contract Dengue
byline: Eight Public Health Inspectors (PHIs) attached to the Colombo District, who are actively engaged in dengue control operations, have contracted dengue, the Public Health Inspectors’ Association said.

title: Heatwave linked to more than 5,000 deaths in Germany, RKI says
byline: Germany has recorded an estimated 5,120 heat-related ​deaths so far this year, ‌most of them in late June when weekly average temperatures far exceeded ​20 degrees Celsius, the Robert ​Koch Institute (RKI) for public health ⁠said on Thursday.

title: China, Taiwan brace for Typhoon Bavi, possibly the most powerful storm in years
byline: China and Taiwan were bracing for possibly the most destructive tropical storm in years as Typhoon Bavi churned southeast of Taiwan ​on Thursday, with winds near 200 kph (124 mph), and as parts of China were still reeling from Typhoon Maysak.

title: Amnesty International says Israel ‘wiping out families’ in Lebanon
byline: The London-based rights group has accused Israel of “wiping out families” in its attacks on Lebanon, and called for the attacks to be treated as “war crimes”.

title: Negombo Prison declared crime scene, no longer suitable for housing inmates
byline: The prison authorities determined that the Negombo Prison premises, which were damaged during the recent unrest, were no longer suitable for housing inmates.

title: India, Australia sign nuclear and defence pacts to bolster Indo-Pacific ties
byline: India and Australia on Thursday signed a set of major agreements covering civil nuclear energy, maritime security and critical minerals, as Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his Australian counterpart Anthony Albanese underlined the importance of their partnership in ensuring a peaceful Indo-Pacific. After wide-ranging talks, the two sides unveiled a joint declaration on defence and security

title: UN praises Sri Lanka’s green initiatives, opens doors for new climate financing
byline: Sri Lanka has gained international recognition for its climate action initiatives and environmental programmes, with the United Nations commending the country’s efforts to engage youth in environmental conservation.

title: Couple transforms AC train coach into ‘honeymoon coupe’, Indian Railways takes action
byline: A viral video showing a train’s First AC cabin decorated like a lavish ‘honeymoon suite’ has prompted the Indian Railways to suspend a ticket checker and order an inquiry.

title: 2,498 qualify for South Korean jobs
byline: The Sri Lanka Bureau of Foreign Employment (SLBFE) has announced the release of the results of the Korean Language Proficiency Test (KLPT), with 2,498 applicants qualifying for employment in South Korea.

title: Public Security Ministry Secretary fined Rs. 2,500 over 2023 road accident
byline: The Secretary to the Ministry of Public Security, retired Senior Deputy Inspector General (DIG) Ravi Seneviratne, was today (9) fined Rs. 2,500 by the Mount Lavinia Magistrate’s Court in connection with a 2023 road accident in Wellawatta.

title: Navy seizes smuggled pharmaceuticals and cosmetics in Kalpitiya
byline: The Sri Lanka Navy, together with the Sri Lanka Coast Guard, has seized a consignment of smuggled pharmaceuticals and cosmetic items during a joint search operation at Sinnapadu beach in Puttalam on July 8.

title: Bonnie Tyler, known for hit song ‘Total Eclipse of the Heart,’ dies age 75
byline: Welsh singer Bonnie Tyler, known for hits such as “Total Eclipse of the Heart,” has died at the age of 75, according to a statement on her website and social media accounts on Thursday.

title: Post-mortems reveal brutal killing of prison officers in Negombo Prison clash
byline: Post-mortem examinations into the deaths of prison officers killed during the recent violence at Negombo Prison have revealed that they were subjected to brutal physical assaults.

title: CEA urges responsible waste disposal at Kataragama Festival
byline: The Central Environmental Authority (CEA) has urged devotees attending the 2026 Kataragama Esala Festival to dispose of waste responsibly and help protect the environment in the sacred city and surrounding areas.

title: New Chairman and members appointed to Public Service Commission
byline: President Anura Kumara Dissanayake has appointed S. A. Nimal Saranatissa as the new Chairman of the Public Service Commission.

title: Confirmed Ebola deaths in DR Congo hit 600
byline: At least 600 people in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) have died from Ebola, as the number of confirmed cases of the illness rose to 1,759, according to government data.

title: National early childhood care week from July 14
byline: The Women and Child Affairs Ministry will mark the National Week on Early Childhood Care and Development from July 14 to 20, with a series of islandwide programmes aimed at promoting the healthy growth and well-being of young children.

title: Second reading of Money Laundering Amendment Bill approved by two-thirds majority
byline: The second reading of the Money Laundering Amendment Bill was approved by a majority of 152 votes in Parliament today.

title: Navy seizes over 60,000 illegal sea cucumbers, arrests 26 in Mannar
byline: The Sri Lanka Navy has seized more than 60,000 illegally harvested sea cucumbers and arrested 26 suspects during a special operation in the South Bar area off Mannar today (9).

title: Conjoined twins successfully separated at Peradeniya
byline: A landmark surgery that successfully separated five-year-old conjoined twins has been hailed as a major achievement in Sri Lanka’s medical history, while also reigniting debate over the capabilities and challenges of the country’s public healthcare system.

title: CAA raids Colombo–Jaffna train restaurant over overpriced bottled water
byline: The Consumer Affairs Authority (CAA) has raided the restaurant compartment of the Colombo–Jaffna express train after uncovering the sale of bottled drinking water above the marked retail price.

title: GMOA warns of misleading social media post
byline: The Government Medical Officers’ Association (GMOA) has warned the public about a fake and misleading post targeting the association that is circulating on social media and messaging platforms.

title: Gunshots account for 14 of 24 deaths in Negombo Prison clash
byline: Post-mortem examinations into the deaths of prison officers killed during the recent violence at Negombo Prison have revealed that they were subjected to brutal physical assaults.
